key_insight: A 190 mm D-gun spray distance produced the densest Cr3C2–NiCr coating and the best corrosion resistance on DSS 2205 in 1 M H2SO4.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing spray distance is a practical lever for improving coating integrity and extending the life of stainless-steel components in acidic industrial service.
method: D-gun sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr onto DSS 2205 at 170, 180, and 190 mm stand-off distances.
Characterized coating morphology and porosity with SEM.
Assessed corrosion behavior in 1 M H2SO4 using OCP, EIS, and potentiodynamic polarization.
evidence_signal: Porosity decreased from 2.84% at 170 mm to 1.38% at 190 mm, and the 190 mm coating showed the lowest corrosion rate of 0.113 mmpy versus 2.60 mmpy for the uncoated substrate.
watch_item: The optimum distance is specific to this powder, substrate, and acid test condition, so process transfer to other setups should be validated experimentally.
paper_title: Effect of spray distance in D-gun sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr coatings on DSS 2205 in acidic environments
